claims.text: rs113993960 is a current dbSNP identifier (not merged into another record).
Earlier identifiers merged into rs113993960: rs199826652.
dbSNP records rs113993960 as variant type 'delins' on NC_000007.14 (GRCh38) with 2 alternate alleles. It is multi-allelic, so each alternate allele is reported separately.
Alternate allele 1: NC_000007.14:g.117559592_117559594del, a deletion (TCTT>T in VCF form).
Alternate allele 2: NC_000007.14:g.117559592_117559594dup, a insertion or duplication (T>TCTT in VCF form).
For alternate allele 1 (TCTT>T), Ensembl VEP predicts inframe_deletion in CFTR (ENST00000003084.11:c.1521_1523del; ENSP00000003084.6:p.Phe508del), impact MODERATE.
For alternate allele 2 (T>TCTT), Ensembl VEP predicts inframe_insertion in CFTR (ENST00000003084.11:c.1523_1524insCTT; ENSP00000003084.6:p.Phe508dup), impact MODERATE.
Ensembl classifies the variant as 'indel' with allele string TCTT/T/TCTTCTT.
Alternate allele 1 (TCTT>T) was not observed in gnomAD v2.1.1 exomes or genomes.
gnomAD v4.1 has no record for 7-117559591-TCTT-T (alternate allele 1).
Alternate allele 2 (T>TCTT) has no gnomAD v2.1.1 record among the 2 MyVariant.info hits for rs113993960.
gnomAD v4.1 has no record for 7-117559591-T-TCTT (alternate allele 2).

ClinVar lists NM_000492.3(CFTR):c.1521_1523del (p.Phe508del) (alternate allele 1) with germline classification 'Pathogenic' for: Cystic fibrosis; BRONCHIECTASIS WITH OR WITHOUT ELEVATED SWEAT CHLORIDE 1, MODIFIER OF; Hereditary pancreatitis; Duodenal stenosis; and 9 more; review status 'practice guideline', 89 submitter(s), allele origin 'de novo;germline;inherited;maternal;paternal;unknown'.

data.title: Genetics and context for precision health in Greater Boston.
Pulmonary Ionocytes Regulate CFTR-Mediated Chloride Transport in Human iPSC-Derived Epithelium.
data.journal: Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol
data.abstract: Pulmonary ionocytes, representing approximately 1% of airway epithelial cells, exhibit high CFTR expression and unique transcriptional markers, including FOXI1, ASCL3, and V-ATPase. Their exact role in human airway physiology is incompletely understood. This study employs induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived airway epithelial models (iPSC-airways) to elucidate the role of FOXI1 in pulmonary ionocyte differentiation and function. CRISPR-Cas9 was used to generate FOXI1-knockout iPSCs, into which a doxycycline-inducible FOXI1-overexpression cassette was introduced. Edited and control lines were differentiated into airway epithelia to evaluate ionocyte formation, epithelial composition, and ion transport. Rescue studies assessed the effects of FOXI1 re-expression in a FOXI1-KO background, and the addition of inducible WT-CFTR ionocytes to F508del/F508del cystic fibrosis (CF) cultures on restoring chloride transport. FOXI1 deletion abolishes ionocyte formation and alters airway epithelial composition, with increased mucus-secreting goblet cells and decreased ciliated cells. Functional assays confirmed ionocytes as key regulators of chloride homeostasis, with FOXI1-deficient airways displaying diminished ion transport. Induction of FOXI1-overexpression restored CFTR-mediated chloride transport. Introduction of WT ionocytes into CF airway models rescued chloride transport deficits, with no rescue observed in vehicle-treated controls lacking ionocyte induction. These findings highlight FOXI1's essential role in pulmonary ionocyte development, airway cell composition, and airway chloride transport. We present a fully manipulable, gene-edited iPSC-derived system that enables investigation of ionocyte biology and function within a human airway context, highlighting them as promising therapeutic targets for respiratory disorders.

data.title: The PDE4 inhibitor tanimilast (CHF6001) activates CFTR function in native and in F508del-expressing airway epithelial cells.
data.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a disorder caused by mutations in the CF transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene, which result in impaired expression and function of the channel that is regulated by cAMP intracellular levels. Therefore, cAMP-elevating agents have been investigated for the treatment of CF, including phosphodiesterase (PDE) inhibitors that act by preventing its degradation by PDE enzymes. Here we characterized the effects of the novel inhaled PDE4 inhibitor, tanimilast (CHF6001), designed to overcome PDE inhibitors systemic adverse effects, on CFTR activation by measuring short-circuit current (Isc) in cellular models expressing native and F508del CFTR (CFBE41o- and normal human bronchial epithelial cells: MucilAir™). Various PDE4 genes (PDE4A, B, D) are expressed in both cell models to different extents. Tanimilast was able to increase Isc in a concentration-dependent manner in both cell models, peaking at 0.2 μM in MucilAir™ expressing either WT and F508del CFTR corrected with a combination of VX445 and VX661 for 24 h. Taken together, these results indicate for the first time that the PDE4 inhibitor tanimilast could enhance, in vitro, the effects of CFTR correctors used in clinical practice.

data.title: Offering prenatal CFTR modulators to prevent cystic fibrosis-related organ damage in utero.
data.abstract: CFTR modulator therapy has drastically improved the prognosis and quality of life for those with cystic fibrosis (CF). CF complications begin to manifest in utero, including meconium ileus, and current regulatory approvals for CFTR modulator therapy does not have a pregnancy indication. Despite this, there have been several documented cases of women taking CFTR modulator therapy during pregnancy with promising results of potential CFTR correction in utero. To report one center's experience offering CFTR modulator therapy to pregnant women for prenatal CF treatment. Eight pregnant women carrying a fetus at risk of having CF were presented with the option of CFTR modulator therapy during pregnancy with extensive counseling on the potential benefits and risks. Records from routine clinical care from prenatal, birth, and perinatal period were collected. Of the eight pregnant women, three intended to take the CFTR modulator, elexacaftor/ tezacaftor/ ivacaftor (ETI), however only two were able, as the third was unable to obtain insurance authorization. In one case, the infant was homozygous for F508del(p.Phe508del, c.1521_1523delCTT, 1653delCTT) variant with signs of worsening bowel obstruction on fetal imaging, however after ETI initiation at 27 weeks he was born without meconium ileus. In the other case of CFTR modulator therapy treatment, the infant carried a CFTR variant of varying clinical consequence, Y1032C (c.3095A>G, p.Tyr1032Cys), and one disease causing CFTR variant. After ETI initiation, ultrasound findings suggestive of bowel obstruction improved and there was no meconium ileus at birth. The family who desired prenatal ETI therapy but was unable to obtain insurance coverage, also had one disease causing variant and one of varying clinical consequence, G622D (c.1865G>A, p.Gly622Asp). Despite fetal imaging concerning for bowel obstruction this infant had no meconium ileus at birth and was classified as CFTR related metabolic syndrome/CF Screen Positive Inconclusive Diagnosis. Of the remaining pregnant women, 3 declined prenatal CFTR modulator therapy, one ultimately had negative prenatal diagnostics, and another terminated the pregnancy. Decisions to treat with prenatal CFTR modulators are complex and influenced by multiple factors including phenotype variability, inconsistent insurance coverage, and uncertain potential risks and benefits. Outcomes of these cases ranged from pregnancy termination to successful reversal of ultrasound findings suggestive of developing meconium ileus.
